name: Dacz Golf
description: Dacz Golf is a high-interaction variant of the classic Golf card game, belonging to the 'Power Card' family (including Cabo and Cambio). Unlike standard Golf, players can use 'Power Cards' drawn from the deck to peek at cards, swap with opponents, or manipulate the layout. The goal remains to have the lowest scoring layout, but the addition of hidden information and unexpected swaps makes it a game of memory, bluffing, and tactical timing. It is known as 'Dacz' in Poland and 'Power Golf' elsewhere.

history.origins: Derived from the traditional game of Golf, the 'Power' variants emerged in the late 20th century. Names like 'Cambio' (Spain) and 'Cabo' suggest a global spread through traveler communities and local evolution.
timeline: Traditional Golf: Simple layout and replacement game.
1990s-2000s: Rise of folk variants adding action powers (Cambio, Pablo, Cumbia).
2010: Commercial versions like 'Cabo' bring the mechanics to a wider audience.
Modern: 'Dacz' remains a popular social variant in Poland.
history.cultural: In Poland, 'Dacz' is a common parlor game. The name is likely a phonetic adaptation of 'Dutch'.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a purely solitaire-like optimization game (Standard Golf) into a highly interactive 'take-that' style game where an opponent's layout is no longer safe from swaps.

setup.players: Two to six players; the game is often best with two to four. Four-card Golf and its power-card variants (Dacz, Cabo, Cambio, Cactus) can in theory be played by two to around eight or more; with eight or more players, two packs are shuffled together. Commercial and folk accounts typically describe play with 2-6 players.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 4 cards face-down in a row. Before play begins, each player may peek at their two outer cards (or two inner, by agreement). The rest of the deck forms the stock; one card is turned up to start the discard pile.

rules.objective: Achieve the lowest total score in your 4-card layout by the end of the round.
rules.gameplay: Turn: draw from stock or top discard. Use drawn card to (a) replace one face-down layout card without looking, discarding the replaced card, or (b) if it is a Jack or Queen drawn from stock, use its power (Jack: swap any two layout cards; Queen: peek at one card) then discard it. Power cards from discard have no power. To end the round: call 'Dacz' instead of drawing; each opponent gets one more turn, then all score.
keyRules: You cannot look at a layout card before replacing it unless a Power (Peek) was used.
Discarded Power Cards cannot have their powers used by the next player (powers only activate when drawn from stock).
Penalty for Caller: If the player who called 'Dacz' does not have the lowest score, they add a +10 penalty (+5 if tied for lowest).

strategy.basic: Memorize your starting two cards. Use Peeks (Queens) to identify your hidden cards or check an opponent's low card. Only swap (Jacks) when you are reasonably sure you are trading a high card for a low one.
strategy.intermediate: Watch which cards opponents draw from the discard pileâ€”this tells you where their low cards are. If an opponent draws a Red King and places it, you know exactly where to aim your next Swap.
strategy.advanced: The 'Match' bluff: discard a card quickly to pretend it matches your hidden card. If done correctly, you can shed high cards early. Timing the 'Dacz' call is critical: do it when you have two 0s or Lows and know opponents are still peeking.
tips: Keep your Red Kings guarded; they are the prime targets for Swaps.
Don't call Dacz unless your total is below 10-15; a 20-point hand is rarely a winner.
If you have a high card you can't get rid of, try to swap it with a known low card of an opponent just before calling Dacz.

variations.name: Cabo (Commercial)
variations.description: Uses specific rhymes: 7/8 (Know your fate - peek own), 9/10 (Know a friend - peek opponent), J/Q (Switch between). King of Diamonds is 0, others 13.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses different power-card rhymes and King values; overrides to be added when implementing Cabo-specific engine.

variations.name: Cambio (Spanish)
variations.description: Often played with Jokers (-5). More aggressive swapping rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Joker values and swap rules differ; overrides to be added when encoding Cambio-specific rules.

variations.name: Cactus (Vancouver)
variations.description: Queens swap any card. 9/10/J peek opponent. 6/7/8 peek own. Call 'Cactus' to end.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Power-card assignment and end-call differ; overrides to be added when implementing Cactus variant.

scoring.description: Lowest total wins. Special values for Kings and certain Face cards depending on the variant.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest cumulative score after a set number of rounds (usually 9 or until someone hits 100).

synthesis.shortDescription: A tactical memory game from the Golf family. Use Jacks and Queens to peek and swap cards, aim for the lowest total, and call 'Dacz' when you're ready to win. Watch out for the Red Kingsâ€”everyone wants them.
